title: DataBall many-file opens must have a bad-file policy and an open report
lead:
`OpenOptions.OnBadFile` chooses how a bad file is handled:
- `Abort` (the default): the open throws, naming the file.
- `Skip`: the other files land, and `OpenReport.Skipped` lists the bad file with its message, plus row, column and value when the error carries them.
If every file is bad, `Skip` still throws. The CLI `import` takes several inputs, `--recursive` and `--skip-bad`.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** strict-cast error fields (db-12 adds `DataBallCastException`, and this slice reads its fields when present); `.ball` sources (db-25).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Split out of db-11 on 2026-10-10. Owner decision (suite alignment doc): "Bad data across files: the caller chooses: abort everything, or skip the bad file and report file / row / column / value."

**Model note (owner, 2026-10-10):** Claude-only relay. Implementer: **Haiku 5.5, high**, a trial. The reviewer and architect models are set at relay start.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/DataBall/OpenOptions.cs`: `BadFilePolicy OnBadFile`.
- `src/DataBall/OpenReport.cs`: `Skipped`.
- `src/DataBall/DataBall.Open.cs`: the policy wraps each source's staging. On abort, no session is left and no path stays in the open-file gate.
- `src/DataBall.Cli/CommandFactory.cs` and `CliApp.cs`: multiple inputs, `--recursive`, `--skip-bad`.
- `README.md` (Library usage, CLI) and `docs/how-it-works.md`.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `Open_BadFile_Abort`: throws naming the file; no session; the gate is clear.
2. `Open_BadFile_Skip`: the other files land; `Skipped` names the bad one.
3. `Open_AllBad_Skip_Throws`.
4. CLI: `Import_ManyInputs_Recursive_SkipBad`.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Spec review.
2. `slicer start` with `--render --strict`. Write tests 1–4, watch them fail.
3. Implement; docs; mutation checks; full Release suite; format.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `dotnet build DataBall.sln -c Release`
- `dotnet test DataBall.sln -c Release`
- `dotnet format DataBall.sln --verify-no-changes`
- CLI smoke: `databall import <dir> --recursive --skip-bad -o s.ball`.
- `slicer check`

sections.heading: Must not change
sections.body:
- A single-file open behaves as before.
- With `Abort`, nothing partial is left.
